articles.title: Flights and train services cancelled in Belgium due to strike
articles.summary: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.
articles.body:
Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and public transport severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures.

All air traffic has been halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem as well as at Charleroi, home to low-cost airlines such as Ryanair.

Underground services have also been halted in capital Brussels, where large numbers of people joined a protest march.

The protest comes as Prime Minister Bart De Wever continues talks with his coalition allies over a budget to cut borrowing costs. King Philippe declined his resignation earlier this month, giving De Wever more time to negotiate.

No flights are taking off or landing at Brussels Airport between 07:00 and 21:00 local time (06:00-20:00 GMT) as a result of the strike by air traffic controllers.

"In total, 404 flights today cannot be operated, which has an impact on more than 50,000 passengers," Brussels Airport spokesperson Jeffrey Franssens said.

Reuters news agency spoke to Florence Faure, a French passenger who had arrived in Brussels from China's capital, Beijing, only to find that her flight to Paris Charles de Gaulle airport had been cancelled.

"Since our luggage was supposed to go on to Paris Charles de Gaulle, we didn't even collect it," she said.

A similar situation has affected Charleroi, where all flights were shown as "scheduled", regardless of the time of departure or arrival.

One passenger told Belgian broadcaster RTBF that she had received no warning and only discovered there were no flights when she arrived at the airport.

Philippe Naime, a teacher, was one of the tens of thousands taking part in the protest march in Brussels.

"Quite simply, no more money is being invested in education, and people are left to fend for themselves. But people do not have the means to do that," he told Reuters.

Public transport, schools and other public services are also facing disruptions.

The Belgian prime minister leads a five-party coalition.

One of its members, the socialist Vooruit, has been refusing to endorse plans agreed by the other four. It wants to raise taxes on the rich and for there to be fewer cuts to pensions and the health sector.

De Wever met King Philippe on Monday for the third update since the impasse.

"While expressing regret over the lack of significant progress, the king encouraged the prime minister to persevere in order to reach an agreement as soon as possible," the royal palace said in a statement.

The leader of one of the country's main unions, FGTB, said the government had alternatives to "dismantling the social protection system".

Bert Engelaar, head of the union, called for "a genuine wealth tax, fair taxation, and the elimination of tax loopholes".

"Political responsibility is not about keeping a government afloat at all costs. It's about knowing when to stop," he added, praising the Vooruit party.

Another union leader, Ann Vermorgen of the CSC, criticised government plans to cut bank holidays when they fall on weekends.

articles.title: Thanksgiving travel forecast: Storms on both coasts could snarl busiest travel days; San Francisco braces for potentially record king tides
articles.summary: Storms on both coasts could disrupt Thanksgiving travel, from a soaking Northeast storm Sunday to a possible major storm on Thanksgiving Day.
articles.body:
Millions of Americans hitting the road and skies for Thanksgiving could run into storms on both coasts, including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day.

On the West Coast, the National Weather Service has issued a coastal flood warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines from Monday through Thursday afternoon, as the year's highest "king tides" coincide with an incoming storm.

A coastal storm is also bringing heavy rain and gusty winds from the mid-Atlantic to New England, which started Sunday night and continued Monday morning. Forecasters are tracking a potentially strong nor'easter for Thanksgiving Day, and an atmospheric river on the West Coast.

"Each of these storms has the potential to trigger major weather delays at major Northeast and West Coast hubs," the Weather Channel said .

Weather hasn't been the only problem facing travelers. Delta Air Lines resolved an outage that caused delays nationwide Sunday, marking the third major disruption to U.S. air travel in nine days.

AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million by car and 5.96 million on domestic flights.

Forecasters are growing more confident that another storm will hit the Northeast on Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and flooding along the coast. The National Hurricane Center said Saturday that it was unlikely to become a tropical or subtropical storm.

In New York City, heavy rain started Sunday and has persisted into Monday, city emergency officials said . The National Weather Service in New York said early Monday to expect 1 to 2 inches of rain, with more in places, and wind gusts of 35 to 45 mph, possibly near 50 mph on the coast. Flooding along the shore could be widespread, with major flooding possible in the most vulnerable spots on Long Island's south shore, the agency said. The storm's timing and track could still change.

New York City Emergency Management said gusty winds Monday could slow flights.

In Florida, more than 16 inches of rain fell near Cocoa Beach over three days, according to AccuWeather, and the St. Johns River near Cocoa hit 18.6 feet Friday, breaking a record set in 1953. Flooding along the river is expected to linger past Thanksgiving.

Tuesday and Wednesday: Atmospheric river in the West, storms in the Southeast

A strong Pacific storm is forecast to hit from Northern California to Washington state starting Tuesday, with rain reaching the Northwest Monday night. The greatest impacts are expected Tuesday and Wednesday, with a risk of flooding and mudslides. Heavy rain, strong winds and mountain snow could cause significant delays along Interstate 5 between Seattle and San Francisco and on mountain routes including I-80. Airports in Seattle and San Francisco could see delays.

"Drivers along I-5 should prepare for heavy rain that can reduce visibility and leave water collecting on the roadway," AccuWeather meteorologist Haley Taylor said. "Travelers heading into the Sierra will face a different challenge, with heavy snow potentially making mountain routes difficult or impassable."

A second, potentially windier storm could strike the same area Wednesday, with the heaviest rain spreading to most of the West Coast on Thursday, the Weather Channel said. The National Weather Service office in Reno said the storms will bring fresh snow to the Sierra Nevada, with periods of difficult travel.

In the San Francisco Bay Area, the storms coincide with potentially record-breaking king tides, the year's highest tides. The National Weather Service has a coastal flood warning in effect until 4 p.m. PT Thursday and calls Tuesday and Wednesday an "extreme" risk for flooding along the bay shoreline, and a high surf warning covers Wednesday on the Pacific coast. The agency said the storm will coincide with the king tides, potentially making flooding worse during Thanksgiving travel.

San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said Sunday city departments are coordinating and "deploying resources" for the storms and high tides. He previously warned of potentially record tides in an X post Saturday.

"We went through the forecast for next week, and we are anticipating high tides and rain that this city has never seen before," he said "This is extremely serious, and we are acting accordingly at the city level. We are going to encourage every resident and business owner to take this extremely seriously. In Marin County, Southern Marin Fire District has urged residents and businesses to "take action now" and prepare for possible road closures and travel disruptions.

In the Southeast, heavy rain and thunderstorms could hit Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. AccuWeather said Wednesday could bring some of the most widespread weather-related travel disruptions before Thanksgiving, particularly in the Southeast, with airline delays expected to expand in Orlando and Miami from Tuesday to Wednesday and in Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday. The National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center has warned of flooding rain along the coastal Carolinas on Wednesday. Delays at those hubs could ripple across the country.

Thanksgiving Day: Possible major storm in the Northeast

Forecasters are increasingly confident that another storm will form off the Southeast coast late Wednesday and move up the East Coast on Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain and strong winds from the mid-Atlantic to New England.

The National Weather Service in Boston called it a "potentially significant coastal storm" for Thanksgiving into Friday, with gusts along the coast possibly topping 50 mph. Very high tides could also bring coastal flooding, the agency said. Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. The storm arrives as king tides continue on both coasts around Tuesday's full moon, which could worsen coastal flooding, the Weather Channel said.

Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. AccuWeather said a brief period of wet snow or sleet is possible in northern New York and New England later Thursday.

That could be a problem for the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which is set to start at 8:30 a.m. Thursday. The parade's giant balloons can't fly if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph, Fox Weather reported .

Forecasters say the storm's exact track and timing could still shift.

The National Weather Service expects the East Coast storm to weaken and move away, though windy conditions and some rain or snow showers could linger in parts of New England and the eastern Great Lakes into the weekend.

Another storm could form in the East during the busy return weekend, while more Pacific storms could hit the West Coast. The Sunday after Thanksgiving is typically one of the busiest travel days of the year.

Forecasters advise travelers to check forecasts for both their departure and arrival cities, and to keep an eye on flight status before heading to the airport.

articles.title: Se acabaron las ayudas del Gobierno para comprar coches electrificados: ¿y ahora qué?
articles.standfirst: Los particulares y autónomos ya no tienen garantizada las ayudas del Plan Auto+, una vez que se ha agotado todo el dinero de la partida. Te contamos qué posibilidades se abren ahora
articles.summary: Los particulares y autónomos ya no tienen garantizada las ayudas del Plan Auto+, una vez que se ha agotado todo el dinero de la partida. Te contamos qué posibilidades se abren ahora
articles.body: Comprar un coche eléctrico o híbrido enchufable con las ayudas del Plan Auto+ ya no es lo mismo que hacerlo hace unos pocos días. El presupuesto destinado a los particulares se ha agotado y las nuevas solicitudes han pasado a una lista de espera. Esto significa que quien compre ahora un coche electrificado puede solicitar la subvención, pero no tiene ninguna garantía de que vaya a recibirla. Y, lo que es más inquietante, tampoco hay de momento un nuevo plan aprobado que permita saber con certeza que esa ayuda se podrá cobrar más adelante. La situación ha cambiado en apenas unos días. El Plan Auto+ nació con una dotación de 400 millones de euros para 2026, repartidos en dos grandes líneas: 350 millones para particulares y 50 millones para empresas y autónomos. Pero la demanda para particulares ha superado las previsiones y las 113.268 solicitudes han ascendido a 358,52 millones de euros. Desde el 19 de noviembre, las nuevas peticiones de los compradores particulares se incorporan a una lista de espera y se atenderán por orden de presentación, siempre que se libere dinero por renuncias o por la denegación de solicitudes anteriores. No obstante, debemos tener muy claro que estar en esa lista no garantiza recibir la ayuda. Y, además, solo se podrá entrar en esta lista de espera hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2026 La situación es parecida para los autónomos. Su partida específica, dotada con 8 millones de euros, también se ha agotado y acumula solicitudes por un importe muy superior al presupuesto disponible. En este caso, el desfase ya rondaba los 12 millones de euros. La única excepción son las empresas. De los 42 millones reservados para ellas todavía quedaban cerca de 13-14 millones de euros, según los últimos datos conocidos. Es la única bolsa que conserva fondos y, al ritmo al que se están presentando las solicitudes, podría agotarse durante la primera mitad de diciembre. Esta es la pregunta que más preocupa a quienes estaban pensando en cambiar de coche. La respuesta es que puedes comprarlo y presentar la solicitud, pero si eres un particular o un autónomo entrarás en una lista de espera y no tienes garantizada la ayuda, por mucho que algún comercial te trate de convencer de que seguro que la recibirás. En la práctica, esto significa que el comprador debería hacer sus cuentas sin dar por descontados los hasta 4.500 euros que hasta ahora podía recibir por un turismo. Que el concesionario ofrezca un descuento comercial es otra cuestión, pero no debe confundirse con la subvención pública. Así que antes de firmar conviene preguntar con claridad si el precio ofertado era el que contaba con las ayudas o no. Que las ayudas continúen o no dependerá de lo que pase después del paso por las urnas, aunque sería de esperar que tanto un ejecutivo de un color como de otro las volvieran a poner en marcha. De momento, el actual Ministerio de Industria ha descartado ampliar la convocatoria de este año, y una de las razones es la de falta de presupuestos. Desde la cúpula actual de este Ministerio sí se ha trasladado la intención de mantener un sistema de incentivos para la compra de vehículos electrificados, e incluso se ha apuntado a la posibilidad de que las nuevas ayudas tengan carácter retroactivo. Pero una intención no es un asunto aprobado y a día de hoy no hay un presupuesto confirmado para 2027, como tampoco fechas, ni condiciones que permitan asegurar que la subvención será una realidad. Además, y en caso de que se aprueben nuevas ayudas, no hay forma de saber cuándo puede tomarse esta medida. Podría llegar en los primeros días del nuevo Gobierno, pero también podría retrasarse varios meses. Hay un precedente que permite entender por qué algunos compradores confían en que las ayudas puedan recuperarse: a comienzos de 2025, el Plan MOVES III quedó interrumpido después de que el Congreso no convalidara el decreto que mantenía su vigencia. Durante esos meses hubo compradores que compraron sus coches sin poder solicitar la subvención. Pero en abril de ese año el Gobierno reactivó el programa, amplió su presupuesto con otros 400 millones de euros y estableció que las compras realizadas desde el 1 de enero de 2025 también podían acogerse a las ayudas. Ahora bien, hay una pequeña diferencia que debes tener en cuenta: en 2025 se trató de recuperar un programa que ya existía y cuya continuidad se había interrumpido durante unos meses. Ahora, en cambio, el presupuesto del Auto+ se ha agotado y será necesario que el próximo Gobierno decida si mantiene el sistema, con qué dinero y desde qué fecha. Otra duda es la de cuánto se tardaría en recibir el dinero, una vez aprobado un nuevo e hipotético plan. El Plan Auto+ se diseñó para simplificar el sistema y centralizar la gestión en el Ministerio de Industria, frente al MOVES III, que dependía de las comunidades autónomas y podía obligar a los compradores a esperar más de un año para cobrar. Sin embargo, el nuevo programa tampoco ha entregado el dinero de forma instantánea, así que es de esperar que unas nuevas ayudas tampoco se puedan cobrar de forma inmediata. Así, tras las enormes dudas que muchos conductores han tenido a la hora de elegir entre un coche híbrido enchufable o eléctrico (entre otras opciones), se suma ahora la de comprarlo como quien da un 'salto al vacío', sin contar con la ayuda pública, o mantener el viejo coche y esperar a conocer qué decide el próximo Gobierno.

articles.title: LinkedIn jobs, secret targets: How Trump's mass layoffs may have opened doors for Chinese spies
articles.summary: Suspected Chinese intelligence operatives are using fake companies and job offers on platforms such as LinkedIn to target current and former US government
articles.body: Suspected Chinese intelligence operatives are using fake companies and job offers on platforms such as LinkedIn to target current and former US government officials, seeking access to sensitive information. Hundreds of suspicious websites identified, according to a report published in the CNN.The network has expanded as thousands of federal employees left government jobs during President Donald Trump's first year back in office, leaving many without adequate guidance on how to identify and avoid such approaches.The suspected operation relies on fake consultancy firms that advertise lucrative research and consulting assignments. Former government officials and private consultants are approached through professional networking platforms and asked to prepare reports on issues related to China and other areas of interest. In some cases, those taking up the assignments do not know who the actual client is.How Trump's mass layoffs created larger pool of potential targetsHundreds of thousands of workers left the federal government through firings, resignations and other means during Trump's first year back in the White House. The departures created a larger pool of unemployed people in the Washington, DC, area, including former officials who held security clearances and had access to sensitive government information.Foreign powers, including China and Russia, responded by stepping up efforts to recruit Americans working in national security, particularly those who had been fired or feared losing their jobs, CNN reported.“We created a vulnerability that was not necessary,” a former senior US intelligence official said, as quoted by CNN, referring to the mass layoffs. “We created access and opportunity to tens of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands, of people without the tools needed to deal with the Communist Party of China.”How suspected Chinese spy network operatesThe fake companies typically use artificial intelligence and stolen identities to create professional-looking corporate websites, according to court documents. They then post vague but well-paying consulting jobs on platforms such as LinkedIn, often seeking people with expertise in China-related issues.Applicants may be asked to prepare research reports for the companies without knowing who is commissioning the work. While an individual report based on publicly available information may reveal little, intelligence officials say a large collection of such reports could help build a detailed picture of US national security policy and its vulnerabilities.The FBI seized 13 websites in June that officials said were linked to fake consulting firms. However, an analysis by CNN and Max Lesser, a senior analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, found several more suspicious websites with links to the seized domains.Lesser has identified more than 100 other web domains that share characteristics with the websites taken down by the FBI. Many remained online months after he publicly revealed them in November 2025, although several have since gone offline.“Those 13 domains are just the tip of the iceberg,” Lesser told CNN. Seizing them is “necessary but not sufficient,” he added, calling for faster action when suspicious domains are reported.The FBI said it was continuing to investigate the activity and take authorised steps to address the threat. China has denied the allegations. A spokesperson for its embassy in Washington said: “I am not familiar with what you mentioned. China opposes vilifying China by peddling the so-called ‘Chinese spy’ narrative.”Former Pentagon official approached with paid assignmentOne of the people approached was Wes Bryant, a former Air Force master sergeant who worked in a Pentagon office focused on reducing civilian harm during military operations. He said he was forced to resign in spring 2025 after criticising cuts to his office.In January 2025, Bryant received an email from someone claiming to represent a Malaysian think tank called MRDA. The sender expressed interest in his military experience and proposed collaboration on regional security issues.After leaving the Pentagon, Bryant decided to test the offer while checking the organisation with former colleagues. He prepared a report on how the Trump administration might approach a security pact with Australia and the UK, using only publicly available information.The purported representative, identified as Lily, paid him $1,200. She later said the unnamed client believed there was “room for improvement” in the report. Bryant suspected this was an attempt to draw out more sensitive information. Former colleagues subsequently told him that MRDA did not exist and that Lily had contacted other Pentagon employees.The Foundation for Defense of Democracies found that MRDA's website used a Chinese-language font and that images posted by one of its representatives carried watermarks from the Chinese social media platform RedNote. Researchers at the University of Toronto's Citizen Lab described the organisation as “likely China-related”, but said they had not found conclusive digital evidence linking it to the Chinese government.Another target, global affairs consultant Andres Loretdemola, said he was contacted on LinkedIn in 2025 by a woman offering up to $1,000 for reports on Russian affairs and geopolitics. He became suspicious after she appeared more interested in his connections with Washington think tanks.Loretdemola shared a recording of their conversation with the FBI. The bureau said the messages he provided were consistent with the pattern of activity described in the warrant used to seize the websites.The use of fake consultancies to approach US officials is not new. In 2018, Singaporean Dickson Yeo set up a fake company and advertised jobs, according to the US Justice Department. Ninety per cent of the resumes he received were from US military and government personnel with security clearances. Yeo was later sentenced to 14 months in prison after pleading guilty to acting as an agent of Chinese intelligence.US officials said the growth of artificial intelligence and the popularity of professional networking platforms have made such operations more effective.A LinkedIn spokesperson said creating fake accounts or misrepresenting one's identity violates the platform's terms of service. “We remain focused on detecting state-sponsored abuse and will continue to enforce our policies against fake accounts,” the spokesperson said as quoted by CNN.The US and its Five Eyes intelligence partners, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the UK, warned in June that information acquired through such schemes could put frontline military personnel at risk, weaken economic prosperity and enable interference in democratic processes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chinese official sentenced to death for leaking 100 intelligence reports, including 35 state secrets
articles.summary: A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for leaking dozens of state secrets to a foreign country, according to a post published on a social media
articles.body: A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for leaking dozens of state secrets to a foreign country, according to a post published on a social media account of Jincheng Press, the publishing arm of China's National Administration of State Secrets Protection."The struggle on the hidden front has never ceased, and intelligence agencies' methods have become increasingly deceptive," the post said, according to the South China Morning Post."We must remain constantly alert to national security risks, strengthen party discipline and awareness of confidentiality, keep our social, personal and friendship circles free of undue influence, strictly observe workplace rules, and guard against being targeted and exploited," it added.The caseBaomiguan, an account overseen by the National Administration of State Secrets Protection, said the official, identified only by his surname, Ma, was recruited by a foreign spy agency while serving abroad.As per the post, Ma became acquainted with an officer of a foreign intelligence agency while serving in a country identified as "Country A". The officer, identified as "Kailin," frequently invited Ma to meet under the pretext of learning Chinese and offered him modest payments in exchange for regular meetings.Over time, their conversations shifted to politically sensitive issues and international affairs, before Kailin began seeking information about the personnel and operations of China's mission in Country A.Kailin later introduced Ma to another intelligence officer, identified as Tang Zheng, who blackmailed him into joining Country B's intelligence service by threatening to expose his past activities to Chinese authorities. Ma eventually agreed to work for the foreign agency.After returning to China, Ma sent more than 100 intelligence reports at Kailin's direction, including 35 classified as state secrets. Before his arrest, he had received over one million yuan (approximately $150,000) in espionage payments through domestic drop-offs and overseas meetings, along with performance-based bonuses.Subsequently, an unspecified court sentenced Ma to death and ordered the confiscation of all his personal propertyChina steps up anti-espionage warnings on social mediaBeijing's state secrecy regulator and the ministry of state security (MSS), the principal intelligence and counter-espionage agency, have increasingly used social media to warn officials against becoming informants or spies for foreign powers.An official account run by the otherwise secretive MSS regularly publishes similar anonymised accounts of officials accused of spying for foreign countries.While many of these cases result in prison sentences, some carry the death penalty. The posts are often widely circulated online and amplified by state media.(With Reuters inputs)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship in Libya as conflict spreads beyond Europe
articles.summary: By Lina Golovnya Nov 23 (Reuters) - Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, the day after a drone strike on a...
articles.body:
Before-and-After Satellite Images of Explosion Aboard Russian Ship in Benghazi

Nov 23 (Reuters) - Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.

Libya's eastern-based government ‌said the corvette, the Merkury, had been docked at the Benghazi naval base.

Zelenskiy published videos on Monday from Ukraine's SBU security service that ‌he said showed the attack, and another drone off Libya hitting the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which he said Moscow had used to transport weapons. The footage, verified by Reuters, ​showed fire erupting and smoke billowing from the ships.

Ukraine's SBU security service said the drones used in Sunday's attack had been launched from a "mother ship" in the region.

While Russia and Ukraine have repeatedly attacked each other's military and commercial shipping in the Black Sea, attacks elsewhere have been rarer.

The SBU said the operation showed that the Russian navy had "no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea".

Zelenskiy's post on Telegram was the first official acknowledgement that Ukraine has carried out an attack ‌in Libya. He said Russia had tried, but failed, ⁠to counter the attack on the corvette.

He said a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter had also been destroyed, adding: "We continue operations in designated waters." Russia's Defence Ministry did not immediately comment.

EASTERN LIBYA HAS MILITARY TIES TO RUSSIA

After a civil war, eastern Libya ⁠is controlled by military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose Libyan National Army has ties with Russia, while the west is controlled by an internationally recognised Government of National Unity based in Tripoli.

The Institute for the Study of War said the Merkury had stopped over for several days, under a cooperation agreement, to refuel and resupply as it escorted ​Russian ​cargo ships that can carry military supplies en route to Russia.

Osama Hamad, prime minister ​of Libya's eastern-based government, said he had asked the UN ‌to investigate "suspicions that the boats had been launched from western Libya" and to verify the presence of Ukrainian military experts there. No comment was immediately available from the Tripoli government.

Russia's Transport Ministry said in March that Ukrainian naval drones launched from Libya had attacked the Arctic Metagaz, which was carrying liquefied natural gas from Murmansk. Libya's maritime agency said the vessel had sunk between Libya and Malta after catching fire. Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for that attack.

GULF OF FINLAND DRONE ATTACK ON RUSSIAN SHIP

On Saturday, a drone attack set fire to another Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, operated by the Russian defence logistics ‌firm Oboronlogistika, in international waters in the Gulf of Finland.

The Finnish military said it was ​likely to have been carried out by Ukraine, although Kyiv did not immediately comment. All ​16 crew were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship, one slightly ​injured.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov answered a question about the attack by saying there was a "dangerous trend of increasing terrorist activity" in ‌the Baltic Sea. He said Moscow hoped adjoining states would ​warn Kyiv off such operations.

Russian, Estonian and ​Finnish vessels fought the fire after the Sparta II drifted into Finnish waters, and a Russian ship began towing it away on Sunday.

US-backed talks between Russia and Ukraine resumed this month after a nine-month hiatus in an effort to end the war, Europe's biggest since World War ​Two, albeit with little result so far.

Mykola Bielieskov of ‌the National Institute for Strategic Studies in Kyiv said Ukraine was looking to strengthen its position with "horizontal escalation".

"Since neither side is able ​to compel the other to accept terms of settlement through the battlefield only, both try to find new ways to pressure each ​other," he said.

(Reporting by Lina Golovnya; Editing by Daniel Flynn and Kevin Liffey)

articles.title: 'Chapo Isidro': Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
articles.summary: Eight suspects are arrested after firing on soldiers trying to re-establish order following the arrest of 'El Chapo Isidro'.
articles.body:
Mexican soldiers have detained eight alleged members of a drug cartel whose leader was arrested on Friday, sparking a wave of violence in northern Sinaloa state.

The Mexican defence ministry said the soldiers were shot by the suspects on Sunday while on patrol in the town of Sinaloa de Leyva, trying to re-establish order in the wake of the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

Meza Flores, also known as "Chapo Isidro", was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list and had managed to evade capture for years.

The ministry said the eight had also been involved in the retaliatory violence unleashed by Meza Flores's cartel in the hours after his arrest on Friday.

In a statement published on social media , the ministry of defence said that one of the detainees was under age.

It added that its special forces had seized six vehicles as part of their operation, two of which had been fitted with bullet-proof armour and gun turrets.

The US Department of Justice described Friday's arrest of Meza Flores as "a spectacular military operation" and congratulated Mexico's military and special forces on his capture.

It said that the US Homeland Security Task Force had supported the Mexican military and praised the "bilateral effort".

Mexico's defence ministry said its special forces had used stealth and surprise to reach the home of the wanted man.

They also established a security perimeter to prevent Meza Flores from escaping and cartel reinforcements from arriving.

Nevertheless, a bloody firefight ensued.

Along with Meza Flores, his second-in-command, known as "Serafín", and his financial operator, were also arrested and quickly transferred by air to Mexico City.

As news of their arrest spread, members of their cartel erected barricades on major roads and set cars and some shops alight.

There were also reports of shoot-outs between the security forces and cartel members.

The prosecutor's office in Sinaloa says 17 people, four of them members of the Mexican security forces, were killed as a result of the violence on Friday and early Saturday.

US Assistant Attorney General A Tysen Duva has described Meza Flores as "the most dangerous man in Mexico".

"For decades Meza Flores has promoted the terrorist objectives of the Sinaloa cartel," Duva said, accusing him of "flooding the United States with deadly substances".

The 44-year-old is believed to have started his criminal career with the Juárez cartel decades ago.

He later moved on to become the right-hand man of the leader of the Beltrán Leyva Organisation, a drug gang once allied to the Sinaloa cartel before the two groups split and became bitter enemies.

As early as 2013, the US Treasury identified Meza Flores as the leader of his own drug-trafficking organisation, named after him.

The US Treasury said at the time, that the Meza Flores drug trafficking organisation was responsible for "the distribution of large quantities of methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and cocaine to the United States".

It added that the turf war between the Meza Flores cartel and the Sinaloa cartel had "resulted in the quadrupling of drug-war killings" in between 2009 and 2013.

According to think tank Insight Crime , Meza Flores himself kept a low profile over the last decade while continuing to run his cartel out of Guasave, in Sinaloa state.

The head of the US Drug Enforcement Administration said that his capture was a "significant blow to a ruthless criminal organisation that has used extreme violence to traffic deadly drugs, including fentanyl, a designated weapon of mass destruction, into American communities".

His arrest, and the co-operation between US and Mexican officials which led to it, will be seen as a win for the government of Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Sheinbaum has stressed that she is keen to work with the US authorities to capture high-profile target as long as Mexican's sovereignty is respected.

articles.title: Navy, Coast Guard plan Rs 15,000 crore deal for 76 helicopters to replace ageing Cheetah, Chetak fleet
articles.summary: The Indian Navy and Coast Guard are planning to acquire 76 new utility helicopters worth around Rs 15,000 crore to replace their ageing Cheetah and Chetak
articles.body: The Indian Navy and Coast Guard are planning to acquire 76 new utility helicopters worth around Rs 15,000 crore to replace their ageing Cheetah and Chetak fleets. The proposal is part of India's wider effort to modernise its military helicopter inventory through indigenous manufacturing and partnerships with foreign manufacturers.According to news agency ANI citing defence sources, the Indian Navy will acquire 51 helicopters, while the Coast Guard will get 25.The project is expected to be discussed at a high-level defence ministry meeting and will be pursued under the Buy and Make (Indian) category of the defence acquisition procedure, with Indian companies partnering with foreign original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) to manufacture the helicopters domestically.The proposed helicopters will belong to the 5-tonne-plus category and are intended to replace the forces' ageing fleet of Cheetah and Chetak light helicopters. The procurement comes amid operational issues with the existing twin-engine choppers, which are used for reconnaissance, surveillance, search and rescue and other maritime operations.The naval procurement is part of a larger effort by India's three defence services to replace their ageing helicopter fleets. The Army and Air Force are separately planning to acquire 400 light helicopters, with 200 to be manufactured by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and the remaining 200 by private-sector companies in partnership with foreign manufacturers, defence sources told ANI.The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) has recently cleared the programme for the 200 helicopters to be manufactured by private-sector companies, with a tender expected to be issued soon. The move is aimed at expanding private-sector participation in military helicopter manufacturing while building domestic production capabilities through partnerships with foreign original equipment manufacturers.Separately, the Indian Navy is planning to acquire 60 Utility Helicopters Marine (UH-M) from HAL, which is developing the platform indigenously. The Navy had earlier planned to procure 111 naval light utility helicopters, but the programme failed to make significant progress.Potential contenders for 76 naval helicoptersUnder the proposed model, Indian companies are expected to collaborate with foreign helicopter manufacturers to produce the platforms in the country.Italy's Leonardo could be among the potential contenders for the Indian Navy and Coast Guard's helicopter requirement, with its AW169M being positioned for the naval utility helicopter programme.Adani Defence and Leonardo signed a strategic partnership in February 2026 to establish a helicopter manufacturing ecosystem in India, covering the AW169M and AW109 TrekkerM platforms. The collaboration envisages domestic manufacturing, maintenance and support capabilities.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he resigned; Huang says: I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process
articles.summary: Jensen Huang is back in charge at Nvidia, less than two weeks after he quit the company he co-founded.
articles.body: Jensen Huang is back in charge at Nvidia, less than two weeks after he quit the company he co-founded. The chipmaker's board has voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately. The board said a series of meetings with Huang left it satisfied with his candour and his ability to lead. It added that input from senior levels of the US government gave it confidence his return poses no national security risk. The move is a complete U-turn from last week, when the same board said it had no plans to bring him back.Huang resigned on November 12, ending a 33-year run as CEO. His exit came days after Nvidia said it would investigate reports that he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Those reports linked him to a woman US officials believe was recruited by China's spy agency. CFO Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO.Nvidia's board reversed course after talks with Huang and Washington"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," said Harvey C Jones, chair of the board. Jones, who stays on as chair, also thanked Kress for her work as interim CEO. She will continue as executive vice president and CFO.Only last Tuesday, Jones opened Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call by saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". The company had also hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Huang, meanwhile, posted on X that he would be honoured to return if the board wanted him. Tech figures including Elon Musk had publicly called for his reinstatement.Huang kept his first statement since the decision humble. "I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," he said. He thanked the board, Jones and Kress, along with employees, shareholders, partners and his family. "I can't wait to get back to work," he added.The investigation into Jensen Huang will still run its courseHuang's return does not end the probe. A committee made up only of independent directors, working with independent counsel, is looking into the foreign intelligence reports. The board said the investigation will proceed to its conclusion. Huang has said he fully supports it and will cooperate.Nvidia is also adding new layers of oversight. The board recently set up a National Security and Export Control Committee, again made up only of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. It is bringing in counsel with national security experience, who will hire specialist advisers of their own. The company has also started a search for a new Chief Compliance Officer, who will report to the board's Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.Nvidia said it will keep cooperating with ongoing government investigations. Huang and general counsel Tim Teter are scheduled to answer questions from US House committees behind closed doors on December 1 and 2.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: 'They were all asleep': Ukrainians describe deadly overnight Russian apartment strike
articles.summary: Eleven people were killed when Russia attacked a block of flats near Kyiv, causing a whole section to collapse.
articles.body:
All that was left of Tetiana's flat after the Russian strike was one outer wall with a satellite dish still clinging to it.

A drone hit her apartment block in Dymer, near Kyiv, before dawn on Sunday, killing 11 of her neighbours.

Tetiana wasn't home. She spent the night in a nearby village, celebrating her 60th birthday.

"I have no flat any more. It's gone. What can I say?" she wondered the next day, as she stood among the anxious crowd gathered waiting for news of neighbours and relatives. "Yesterday was my birthday – so today it's like I've been born again."

The bodies of the victims, including a teenager, have now been pulled from the ruins.

A whole section of the five-storey block was destroyed, collapsing into a mound of rubble which rescuers climbed to search for survivors.

On Sunday evening, they managed to find a seven-year-old boy, Davyd, alive and able to direct them to where he was trapped.

He's now being cared for in hospital, as well as Valentyna, a 79-year-old woman who was rescued almost a full day after the deadly strike. Caught between concrete slabs, still in her bed, she too had managed to call the emergency teams towards her.

Two residents of the building are still officially missing, though most of the wreckage has now been cleared.

The Russian attack happened as Ukrainian naval drones sank a Russian warship, the Merkury, which had docked for refuelling in Libya. The Angara cargo ship, which Kyiv says is used for military logistics and is on US and Ukrainian sanctions lists, was also hit.

"We are responding to Russia's aggression," President Volodymyr Zelensky said, calling both vessels legitimate targets.

He said the block of flats in Dymer, a village in the Kyiv region, had been struck by a Russian Shahed drone, possibly one of the jet-powered drones that travel at extremely high speeds and have been launched at Ukraine in large numbers in recent days.

Zelensky stressed that such weapons used foreign components, and he called for sanctions to be tightened.

"Every country and every leader who helps maintain pressure on the aggressor helps protect human life," he said.

But even hours after the initial attack, the danger had not passed.

Russia increasingly uses its drones to hit Ukraine just as rescuers go to work. They're known as "double-tap" attacks, and often deadly.

It makes the work of searching for survivors, which now happens every single day, extremely perilous.

In Dymer, all rescue work had to stop multiple times on Sunday as more Russian drones were detected overhead.

The emergency services, as well as residents and the press, had only moments to clear the scene and rush for shelter as Ukrainian fighter jets began shooting drones out of the sky.

Many people huddled in an underground kindergarten, decked out with children's paintings and balloons, the safest place around.

In one corner, we found its director crouching on a tiny child's chair.

Natalia had rushed to the scene minutes after hearing the explosion just after 05:00.

One of them, 12-year-old Kira, was later confirmed to have been killed together with her mother.

"So many people," Natalia said quietly. "It happened at night. Had it been daytime, then people might have been out at work. Or the shops. But they were all asleep."

At one point, a mother - held up by emergency workers - directed rescuers towards her son. "Go gently," she urged them, as they carried him out on a stretcher.

He had only come home on Saturday night to collect some papers for college, his cousin said. He wasn't even supposed to be here.

The number of civilians casualties here has been surging in recent weeks.

On Sunday, in the Kyiv region alone, four people were killed in two other deadly attacks - one on a supermarket. A young teacher was among the dead.

"This is the tactic of Russian Federation," Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration told us at the scene. "They are trying to make us scared. To stop Ukraine fighting. But they cannot do this with us."

But the aerial attacks - and retaliation - are now almost non-stop and their scope is widening.

Additional reporting by Mariana Matveichuk, Marianne Baisnée and Matthew Goddard
